items.title: ERS/ESRS clinical practice guideline for continuous positive airway pressure for the treatment of adult obstructive sleep apnoea.
items.abstract: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is the primary treatment for obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), although its effectiveness may vary across OSA subtypes. This joint European Respiratory Society (ERS)/European Sleep Research Society (ESRS) clinical practice guideline evaluates CPAP's impact on patient-centred and prognostically relevant outcomes, comparing it to no or sham treatment in different OSA subgroups. The joint ERS/ESRS Task Force consisted of experts in pulmonology, cardiology and respiratory sleep medicine, patient representatives and methodologists. Questions were formulated using the PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes) framework. A systematic review assessing the effects of CPAP on critical outcomes was performed. The certainty of evidence for all outcomes was assessed using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach. Consensus on the direction and strength of the recommendation was informed by Evidence-to-Decision frameworks and achieved through discussions and voting. The Task Force generally suggests CPAP treatment for OSA because of its beneficial effects on sleepiness, other patient-reported outcomes and blood pressure (conditional recommendations). CPAP is recommended in patients with excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) (strong recommendation). Additional specific conditional recommendations are given for patients with moderate-to severe OSA, the elderly, and patients with arterial and treatment-resistant hypertension. The Task Force suggests either CPAP or no treatment in patients without EDS (but taking into account other OSA-related symptoms), in patients with atrial fibrillation with the aim of reducing its recurrence and in patients with impaired glucose metabolism to improve glycaemic control. CPAP is an effective treatment for adults with OSA. However, recommendations for its use vary across different patient subgroups.

items.title: Patient-Reported Benefits of Acoramidis Across Genotypes in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: KCCQ and EQ-5D-5L Outcomes From ATTRibute-CM.

Left Ventricular Functional Improvement is Associated With Lower Morbidity and Mortality During Long-Term Mechanical Circulatory Support: An STS Intermacs Analysis.
items.abstract: A subset of patients with advanced heart failure (HF) supported with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) demonstrate significant improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), but the impact of such functional improvement on clinical outcomes is unclear. We analyzed adults in the STS-Intermacs registry who underwent continuous-flow LVAD implantation (2006-2017) and had echocardiographic data ≥6 months post-implant. Post-LVAD myocardial function was defined by the maximum LVEF after ≥6 months of support and categorized as <40% vs ≥40% and into finer strata. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, clinically significant sustained cardiac arrhythmia, hepatic and renal dysfunction, CVA/TIA, right HF during follow-up, and HF hospitalization. Incidence rates and incidence rate ratios were calculated during 6-month landmarked follow-up through 5 years, and associations were assessed using landmarked multivariable Cox models. Among 9,518 eligible patients (age 56.6±13.2 years, 21.4% female), 1,131 (12%) achieved LVEF ≥40% over a median 27.0 months of follow-up. Compared with LVEF <40%, LVEF ≥40% was associated with lower adjusted incidence rates of death (adjusted IRR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-0.98), arrhythmia (0.59, 0.48-0.72), hepatic dysfunction (0.58, 0.35-0.97), and HF hospitalization (0.65, 0.51-0.82), whereas adjusted differences in right HF and renal dysfunction were not significant. In adjusted time-to-event analyses, LVEF ≥40% was independently associated with lower hazards of all-cause mortality (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.71-0.96), HF hospitalization (0.63, 0.50-0.80), cardiac arrhythmia (0.69, 0.58-0.83), and hepatic dysfunction (0.57, 0.37-0.88). Across ordered LVEF strata, higher LVEF was associated with progressively lower risks of death and HF-related events. In a large multicenter LVAD cohort, LV functional response to durable support spanned a spectrum, with ∼1 in 8 (12%) durable LVAD recipients achieving a maximum post-implant LVEF ≥40% after ≥6 months of support. Higher post-implant LVEF was independently associated with improved survival and fewer HF-related events. These findings support viewing myocardial improvement during LVAD support as a clinically meaningful target that affects positively the outcomes of patients while being on mechanical support.

items.title: Continuous Vutrisiran Reduces Cardiovascular Events and Hospitalizations in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy in the HELIOS-B One-Year Open Label Extension.
items.abstract: Vutrisiran significantly reduced the risk of all-cause mortality and recurrent cardiovascular (CV) events vs placebo in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) in the phase 3 HELIOS-B study (NCT04153149). Here, we report the long-term impact of vutrisiran on hospitalizations and urgent heart failure (HF) visits from the ongoing HELIOS-B open-label extension (OLE). In HELIOS-B, patients received vutrisiran 25 mg or placebo every 3 months over a 33-36-month double-blind period, followed by a 24-month OLE continuing with vutrisiran (continuous treatment), or if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran (delayed treatment). Hospitalizations and urgent HF visits were analyzed through 48 months (12 months of the OLE) in the overall and monotherapy (not receiving tafamidis at baseline) populations, and the baseline tafamidis subgroup. Of 654 participants, 466 entered the OLE. Continuous vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause hospitalizations vs delayed treatment in the overall population (relative rate ratio [RRR] 0.71, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.62-0.82, P<0.001) and the monotherapy population (RRR 0.60, 95% CI 0.50-0.72, P<0.001). Continuous vutrisiran also significantly reduced the risk of CV hospitalizations, HF hospitalizations, and non-CV hospitalizations vs delayed vutrisiran in the overall and monotherapy populations, and urgent HF visits in the overall population and baseline tafamidis subgroup. Continuous vutrisiran reduced the risk of CV events and hospitalizations relative to patients originally randomized to placebo in HELIOS-B. Many treatment effects were of greater magnitude at 48 months vs 36 months with continuous vutrisiran, highlighting the benefits of earlier diagnosis and treatment.

items.title: Advances in CAR-T and CAR-NK cell therapy in follicular lymphoma: a review.
items.abstract: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the most common indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma and is characterized by prolonged survival but recurrent relapses. The unmet need is greatest among patients with high-risk disease, including progression of disease within 24 months of first-line immunochemotherapy (POD24), double-refractory disease, histologic transformation, and exposure to multiple previous lines of therapy. In pivotal single-arm studies enrolling heavily pretreated patients, CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies produced overall response rates of 86-97% and complete response rates of 68-94%, with durable disease control in a substantial proportion of patients. However, autologous CAR-T therapy is limited by individualized manufacturing, the potential need for bridging therapy, intensive monitoring, unique toxicities, and restricted access outside specialized centers. This review summarizes the efficacy and safety of approved CAR-T products in relapsed/refractory FL, explains how differences in receptor architecture and costimulatory signaling may affect cellular kinetics and toxicity, and discusses emerging alternative targets, dual-target constructs, combination strategies, and CAR-natural killer (CAR-NK) cell platforms. CAR-NK cells represent a promising investigational off-the-shelf platform; however, current clinical evidence is derived predominantly from early-phase studies involving heterogeneous B-cell malignancies, with limited FL-specific data. Their efficacy, durability, safety, and scalability in FL therefore remain to be established in dedicated clinical studies.

items.title: A renal cyst-clear cell renal cell carcinoma comorbidity analysis identifies a FOXM1-positive epithelial COL6A1-CD44 axis that remodels fibroblasts.
items.abstract: Renal cystic conditions are heterogeneous. We used a broad renal cyst-associated disease-gene framework to identify molecular programs shared with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), without modeling a specific cystic disorder or direct cyst-to-cancer progression. We identified 237 shared genes between renal cyst disease and ccRCC (TCGA-KIRC), performed functional enrichment, Mendelian randomization, and built a random survival forest (RSF) risk score benchmarked against published signatures and immunotherapy cohorts. Single-cell (Scissor, SCENIC, scTenifoldKnk virtual FOXM1 knockout) and spatial transcriptomics (RCTD, CellChat) were integrated with fibroblast subclustering and oncoPredict drug screening. Candidate FOXM1 inhibitors were prioritized by docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics, with isovitexin validated functionally. The shared program was enriched for epithelial development and ECM remodeling. Two direction-specific Mendelian randomization analyses supported associations between genetic liability to kidney cancer and related renal cystic phenotypes. The RSF score showed robust prognostic discrimination across cohorts and separated immunotherapy outcomes. High-risk tumors were enriched for Tregs, B cells, and fibroblasts. FOXM1+ malignant epithelium represented the high-risk state, with elevated CNV burden and regulon activity; virtual FOXM1 knockout identified COL6A1 and CD44 among 129 significant non-target perturbation hits. Convergent single-cell and spatial analyses nominated a COL6A1-CD44 communication axis associated with fibroblast remodeling, with F5_SFRP2 + fibroblasts as the most plausible receiving state. These fibroblasts showed ECM-remodeling, adverse prognosis, and pathway activation. Isovitexin emerged as a lead FOXM1-targeting compound, significantly suppressing ccRCC proliferation, migration, and invasion. These findings support a testable communication model involving FOXM1+ epithelium, COL6A1-CD44 and F5_SFRP2+ fibroblasts. The in vitro results also support further evaluation of isovitexin in ccRCC.

items.title: Enhancing neoadjuvant immunotherapy for locally advanced rectal cancer via an injectable thermosensitive hydrogel system with multipathway macrophage immunomodulation.
items.abstract: Conventional surgery for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) faces challenges including difficult sphincter preservation and high recurrence rates. Neoadjuvant immunotherapy holds promise for addressing this clinical challenge by reducing the preoperative tumor burden and activating immune memory. However, the benefit remains limited for most patients, who present with the pMMR/MSS subtype, a so-called "immunosuppressive tumor". Therefore, we developed an injectable thermosensitive hydrogel (OXA/αCD47/CpG@PLEL) that, upon transanal minimally invasive injection, achieves precise location and in situ sustained release of oxaliplatin (OXA), anti-CD47 antibody (αCD47), and CpG oligodeoxynucleotides (CpG) at the tumor site for neoadjuvant immunotherapy of LARC. Released OXA induced cancer cell immunogenic cell death, accompanied by exposure of the calreticulin "eat me" signal to macrophages, while αCD47 blocked the CD47-SIRPα "don't eat me" pathway between cancer cells and macrophages, and CpG further activated macrophages. These effects synergistically enhanced phagocytosis by macrophages, while the combination of αCD47 and CpG promoted M1-type polarization of macrophages. In an orthotopic mid-low LARC mouse model, a single preoperative dose of this hydrogel effectively enhanced macrophage antitumor activity. In addition, it promoted dendritic cell maturation and the subsequent systemic CD8 + T-cell response. This triple-action approach significantly reduced the tumor burden and in turn facilitated surgical resection, minimized organ damage, and suppressed postoperative recurrence, culminating in markedly prolonged survival. More importantly, tumor-free mice after initial treatment resisted tumor re-exposure, which was accompanied by increased effector memory T cells. This injectable thermosensitive hydrogel with multipathway macrophage immunomodulation may enhance innate and adaptive immune responses through minimally invasive intervention, precise drug delivery, and long-term regulation, representing a potential synergistic neoadjuvant immunotherapy strategy for LARC.

items.title: A comparative evaluation of Bayesian model-assisted two-stage designs for Phase I/II clinical trials.
items.abstract: The primary goal of a two-stage Phase I/II trial is to identify the optimal dose for the following large-scale Phase III trial. Conventional Phase I designs focus on the maximum tolerated dose (MTD), assuming that efficacy increases monotonically with dose. However, this assumption may not hold for novel therapies such as immunotherapies and targeted agents, where efficacy can plateau or decline at higher doses. In such cases, the optimal biological dose (OBD)-finding designs are more appropriate. In practice, several recommended Phase II doses (RP2Ds) are typically selected after Phase I for further evaluation in Phase II, where dose optimization designs assess toxicity and efficacy outcomes to support "go/no-go" decisions. The final recommended Phase III dose (RP3D) is then chosen from the RP2Ds meeting these criteria. We compared fifteen Bayesian model-assisted two-stage designs, combining five designs (BOIN, TITE-BOIN, BF-BOIN, BOIN12, and TITE-BOIN12) for dose finding with three designs (TS, BOP2, and TOP) for dose optimization, through extensive simulations under fixed and random scenarios, with and without the existence of the OBD. Our results show that BOIN12 and TITE-BOIN12 achieve better overdose control and RP2D selection, while BOP2 and TOP consistently outperform TS in RP3D selection.

items.title: PD-1 inhibitor-associated Sicca syndrome mimicking Sjögren's disease successfully managed without immunotherapy withdrawal.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are increasingly associated with a broad spectrum of immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including rheumatic manifestations. We report a case of ICI-associated sicca syndrome (ICI-S) mimicking Sjögren's disease, with a brief literature review. The patient was a 70-year-old man with BRAF-mutated metastatic melanoma who developed inflammatory arthralgias followed by parotid and submandibular enlargement, severe xerostomia, and xerophthalmia, during pembrolizumab therapy. Treatment was withheld and low-dose glucocorticoids (GC) initiated, with rapid improvement of joint symptoms and gland swelling, although marked xerostomia persisted. The diagnostic work-up revealed elevated inflammatory markers and positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA), with negative anti-SSA/SSB. Salivary gland ultrasound showed grade 3 changes (OMERACT) and PET-CT confirmed bilateral sialadenitis. Minor salivary gland biopsy demonstrated T-cell-predominant lymphocytic infiltrate without CD20+ B cells, supporting an ICI-S rather than primary Sjögren's disease. Pembrolizumab rechallenge triggered a flare of sialadenitis and arthritis, controlled with GC reintroduction plus hydroxychloroquine and supportive measures. This case provides educational insights into the diagnostic differentiation between ICI-S and primary Sjögren's disease, supporting early recognition and appropriate management without compromising oncologic treatment.

items.title: Hepatitis B and C Virus Among Prisoners in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo estimate the pooled prevalence and identify transmission drivers of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections among incarcerated populations in sub-Saharan Africa.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following a search encompassing Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and free-text terms from database inception through February 2025. Data were synthesized from 26 studies involving 77,760 prisoners across sub-Saharan Africa. A random-effects model was used to calculate pooled prevalence estimates, assess regional variation, and evaluate odds ratios (OR) for potential transmission risk factors.ResultsThe overall pooled prevalence was 13.0% for HBV and 8.0% for HCV among prisoners. Significant regional disparities were observed, with West Africa presenting the highest HBV burden (16.3%) and East Africa showing the highest HCV burden (8.8%). Key independent predictors of infection included sharing sharp objects (OR, 1.98), tattooing (OR, 1.92), and intravenous drug use (OR, 1.38).ConclusionIncarcerated populations in sub-Saharan Africa experience a high burden of viral hepatitis driven by parenteral exposure and high-risk sexual interactions. Addressing these gaps requires targeted screening, comprehensive harm reduction, condom provision, and integrating prison health services into national elimination strategies.
items.journal: Journal of the International Association of Providers of AIDS Care

items.title: Bone missile injury with an intact host femur after high energy road traffic trauma: a case report.
items.abstract: A 28 year old woman presented with local wound infection two weeks after sustaining an anterior thigh laceration in a high energy motorbike crash that killed the co-riding motorcyclist. X-ray revealed a non-identifiable radio-opaque fragment and computed tomography identified a bony foreign body deep in the thigh adjacent to the femoral vessels, with the host femur intact. A 6 x 3 cm fragment of cortical bone was removed at surgery. Histopathology and genetic studies to confirm its origin were not feasible in this resource-limited setting, but an intact host femur suggested it originated from the deceased rider. The wound healed by secondary intention, HIV and hepatitis serology were negative at 6 weeks. This case highlights the unusual occurrence of a bone missile and the importance of early advanced imaging and prompt post-exposure prophylaxis following high-energy, multi-victim trauma.

items.title: Molecular biophysics of viral proteins: From mechanistic insights to microbiological and clinical applications.
items.abstract: Viral proteins are dynamic molecular machines that couple molecular-scale events to microbiological phenotypes, including host-cell tropism, entry efficiency, environmental persistence, strain-specific immune escape, and antiviral resistance. In this review, we critically evaluated how experimental, computational, and biochemical approaches define these links and support clinical translation. We organized the evidence around four key observables: Structure, dynamics, mechanics, and thermodynamics. We then assessed which conclusions remained robust across methods and viral families. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, cryogenic electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, calorimetry, all-atom molecular dynamics (MD), coarse-grained MD, structural bioinformatics, artificial intelligence, and biochemical reconstitution were compared in terms of resolution, sampling, assumptions, and validation requirements. Human immunodeficiency virus type 1 and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 were used as data-rich exemplars, but the resulting conclusions were tested against influenza virus, hepatitis B virus (HBV), human papillomavirus (HPV), Ebola virus, adenovirus, bacteriophages, and other systems. Particular attention was given to force-field selection, enhanced sampling, free-energy calculations, convergence, experimentally restrained modeling, and the multiscale relationship between all-atom and coarse-grained simulations. We also examined integrative workflows, the licensed HBV and HPV virus-like particle (VLP) vaccines, emerging dengue and coronavirus VLP platforms, and clinically validated structure-guided antivirals and prefusion-stabilized antigens. The analysis identified where evidence converges, where method-specific biases or limited taxonomic sampling constrain generalization, and which measurements are required to connect a molecular mechanism to infection, transmission-relevant traits, surveillance, or therapeutic performance. This critical, experimentally anchored framework defines the distinctive contribution of the review.

items.title: Effect of Hepatitis B virus X T118N mutant protein in HepG2 cell cycle and apoptosis regulation.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) belongs to Hepadnaviridae family and caused liver infection. HBV infection can develop into hepatocellular carcinoma, one of which is due to presence of HBV X protein (HBx). Some mutations are known to be associated with development of liver carcinoma, for instance HBx K130M/V131I (HBx_KV). In Indonesia, HBx T118N (HBx_T) has been found at similar frequency as the HBx_KV. This study aims to examine the effect of HBx T118N mutant on cell cycle and apoptosis regulation. In this study, analysis of CyclinE, p21, Bax, and Bcl-2 gene expression was performed using RT-qPCR. Cell cycle and apoptosis analysis was done using flowcytometry with PI and Annexin V-PI staining, respectively. Caspase 3 activity assay was performed using CaspACE™ Colorimetric Assay Kit. The presence of HBx_T mutant increased CyclinE expression at 72 h post transfection, similarly to HBx_KV. Both Bax and Bcl-2 mRNA level were also increased HepG2 cells expressing HBx_T in comparison to HBx_KV expression at 72 h post transfection. HBx_T expression in HepG2 cells at 48 h post transfection caused increase of AnnexinV+/PI- and AnnexinV+/PI+ cell populations, as compared to HBx_wt expression. Our data suggests that HBx_T influences cell cycle and apoptosis regulation in slightly different mechanism to HBx_KV. Further investigations are still required to understand HBx_T mutant involvement in development of chronic liver disease and liver cirrhosis.

items.title: Global Sociodemographic Disparities in the Severity of Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis.
items.abstract: Alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) carries high short-term mortality, yet the contribution of sociodemographic factors to disease severity and outcomes is poorly defined. We conducted a prospective cohort study across 30 centers in 14 countries (January 2015-September 2024). We included adults who met National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) criteria for AH. Outcomes included infections, access to liver transplantation (LT), and survival. Mortality was analyzed with Fine-Gray competing-risk models. Among 726 participants (median age, 49 years; 90.1% male), 24.8% had less than secondary education, and 37.6% reported good social support. Severe AH was more frequent in those without secondary education than in those with at least secondary education (97.2% vs. 81.7%; P<0.0001). The 30- and 90-day survival rates were lower among participants without secondary education (66.4% and 50.4%, respectively) than among those with at least secondary education (88.4% and 81.2%, respectively). In adjusted analyses, moderate and good social support were associated with lower mortality (each sHR 0.58, 95% CI, 0.38-0.89 and 0.38-0.94, respectively), as were secondary (sHR 0.48, 95% CI, 0.24-0.97) and tertiary education (sHR 0.44, 95% CI, 0.20-0.97) and corticosteroid use (sHR 0.63, 95% CI, 0.42-0.95). Lower educational attainment and poorer perceived social support were associated with greater AH severity at presentation and higher mortality, independent of clinical risk factors. These findings highlight the need to address social determinants and favor equitable access to evidence-based therapies, including early LT.

items.title: Metastatic Lung Adenocarcinoma to the Uterus Mimicking a Primary Uterine Malignancy: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma is the most prevalent subtype of non-small cell lung cancer and exhibits a high tendency for distant metastasis. However, uterine metastasis with synchronous multiorgan involvement is extremely rare and prone to misdiagnosis due to atypical clinical presentations. To date, fewer than 20 cases of lung adenocarcinoma metastasizing to the uterus have been documented globally, most of which present with typical gynecological symptoms, making our atypical case highly educational and complementary to existing clinical data. Herein, we describe a 77-year-old postmenopausal female patient who initially presented with lumbago and dizziness without typical pulmonary or gynecological symptoms, with an ECOG performance status of 1. Imaging studies raised suspicion of a primary uterine malignancy, but pathological biopsy, immunohistochemistry, and genomic testing ultimately confirmed advanced lung adenocarcinoma with multiorgan metastases (uterus, lung, liver, bone). Molecular analysis identified an EGFR exon 21 p.L858R mutation, and the patient received palliative local radiotherapy combined with osimertinib targeted therapy. During treatment, the patient developed mild radiation-induced fatigue and slight myelosuppression, which were fully relieved after symptomatic supportive care, with no severe unexpected adverse events observed. This case illustrates the atypical metastatic pattern of lung adenocarcinoma, underscores the pivotal role of pathological and immunohistochemical examinations in differentiating primary from metastatic tumors, and offers a reference for managing diagnostically challenging cases. Early and accurate diagnosis coupled with genomic-guided personalized therapy is critical for enhancing quality of life and prognosis in patients with advanced lung cancer.

items.title: Emerging novel therapies for the treatment of hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia.
items.abstract: Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia is the second most common heritable bleeding disorder worldwide, with a prevalence more than twice that of haemophilia, and is the most morbid inherited bleeding disorder of women. As an autosomal dominant vasculopathy due to dysregulated angiogenic signalling, patients with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia develop telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations which cause numerous complications. These complications include moderate-to-severe chronic epistaxis, gastrointestinal bleeding, iron deficiency anemia, and requirement for intravenous iron or red cell transfusion. Additionally, incidence of intracranial haemorrhage is high and morbid non-bleeding complications, such as venous thromboembolism, stroke, and liver disease, are common. Despite this serious disease burden, hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia remains without licensed therapies worldwide. However, many novel, investigational agents targeting vascular and haemostatic systems are now rapidly undergoing formal development specifically in hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia. These agents include the selective AKT1/AKT2 inhibitor engasertib, AKT1-selective inhibitors ATV-1601 and TER-4480, plasminogen siRNA agent ALN-6400, activin receptor-like kinase 1-bone morphogenetic protein receptor type II (ALK1-BMPRII) bispecific clustering antibody DIAG723, and apelin receptor antagonist antibody TX2100. This comprehensive Review provides essential background information and illustrations summarising relevant hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia pathophysiology, followed by focused, detailed discussions of each of the novel agents in development, including the mechanisms, therapeutic rationale, clinical trial programmes, and potential therapeutic effects.

items.title: Somatic Mutation-Informed Transcriptional Architecture of Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multiomics Study Centered on TP53 .
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by extensive somatic mutation heterogeneity, yet the cellular contexts in which recurrent driver mutation-associated transcriptional programs operate remain incompletely defined. In this study, we applied a mutation-informed multiomics framework centered on TP53 to connect somatic mutation status, bulk transcriptional programs, and hepatocyte-like cell states at single-cell resolution. Somatic mutation profiles and transcriptomic data from the TCGA-LIHC cohort were used to construct directional mutation-associated transcriptional signatures, with CTNNB1 retained as a reference driver signature and AXIN1 and ARID1A retained for descriptive comparison. These bulk-derived transcriptional programs were then projected into single-cell RNA sequencing data to evaluate inferred TP53 -associated transcriptional activity across hepatocyte-like populations. TP53 mutation-associated transcriptional programs were enriched in proliferation-related pathways, DNA repair processes, and stress-response programs and were associated with adverse clinical outcomes. At the single-cell level, inferred TP53 -associated transcriptional activity showed heterogeneous distribution across hepatocyte-like populations and was preferentially enriched in putative malignant hepatocyte-like states. Pseudobulk and functional program analyses further supported the association between TP53 -high signature states, cell-cycle activity, DNA repair, stress programs, and altered tumor-cell communication patterns. Integrated prioritization identified CDCA8 , MCM10 , and TRIP13 as representative genes associated with TP53 -related transcriptional programs; these genes should be interpreted as components of a TP53 -associated proliferative transcriptional state rather than as experimentally validated drivers. These findings provide a mutation-informed view of transcriptional architecture in HCC and illustrate how bulk mutation-associated signatures can be integrated with single-cell data to improve biological interpretation of somatic variation.

items.title: Machine learning quantification of hepatobiliary lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio in benign hepatocellular tumors: a feasibility study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility of a machine learning derived semi-automatic quantification of the lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio following hepatobiliary contrast agent injection for the characterization of benign hepatocellular tumors. Precontrast, arterial, portal venous and hepatobiliary phases of liver magnetic resonance images were coregistered, then the liver was automatically segmented by a pretrained U-Net network. Each lesion was then manually segmented on the arterial phase, while different regions of interest were automatically placed in the liver parenchyma (ring shape, circular). Two-dimensional and three-dimensional lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratios were automatically calculated using each different regions of interest and the whole liver volume. All the calculated lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio were compared to a manual lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio and correlated to organic-anion-transporting polypeptide expression. Moreover, the ability of each calculated lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio in classifying the two lesions was investigated. A total of 23 hepatocellular benign tumors were analyzed including nine focal nodular hyperplasias (39 %) and 14 hepatocellular adenomas (61 %). The correlation between each calculated lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio and the manual value was strong (Pearson coefficient ranging between 0.69 and 0.87). Regarding correlation with organic-anion-transporting polypeptide expression, the highest correlation values was obtained with two-dimensional ring region of interest lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio (Pearson coefficient = 0.56). All lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio values were effective in classifying between focal nodular hyperplasia and hepatocellular adenoma, with the best results in terms of inverse Fisher discriminant ratio obtained with ring-shaped region of interest (0.34 2D, 0.28 3D) and uniform liver region of interest (0.28 2D, 0.37 3D). Semi-automatic quantification of the hepatobiliary lesion-to-liver contrast enhancement ratio both using a two- or a three-dimensional approach is a promising tool for benign hepatocellular characterization.
items.journal: Research in diagnostic and interventional imaging

items.title: Transarterial Radioembolization in the Treatment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Combination Strategies.
items.abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of transarterial radioembolization (TARE) using Yttrium-90 (Y-90), a minimally invasive locoregional therapy for HCC patients who are ineligible for surgical resection. A narrative review of the literature was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus databases. Studies focusing on patient selection, technical aspects, dosimetry, safety, oncologic outcomes and combination strategies were included. Clinical guidelines, prospective and retrospective studies, and comparative analyses were synthesized. A total of 43 key publications were synthesized, including landmark randomized controlled trials (SARAH, SIRveNIB, DOSISPHERE-01), recent meta-analyses and current clinical practice guidelines from EASL, AASLD and ESMO. Transarterial radioembolization demonstrates high objective response rates and favorable survival outcomes across Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stages, with a favorable safety profile compared to systemic therapies. Personalized dosimetry approaches significantly improve response rates as demonstrated in the DOSISPHERE-01 trial. Combination strategies with immune checkpoint inhibitors and tyrosine kinase inhibitors show promising synergistic potential, supported by ongoing phase II/III trials including IMMUWIN, ROWAN and EMERALD-Y90. Transarterial radioembolization is a safe and effective locoregional therapy for HCC, with expanding indications including radiation segmentectomy with curative intent, downstaging for transplantation and combination with systemic therapies. Future research should focus on optimal sequencing, personalized dosimetry thresholds and identification of patients who are most likely to benefit from combination approaches.
